evidence:
Tree compared against the closed list in references/staged-task-contract.md. Top level holds exactly instruction.md, task.toml, environment/, solution/, tests/. environment/ holds Dockerfile, assets/seed_data.json and six instructions/*.md notes (contract: 'one or more operating notes'). tests/ holds exactly .dockerignore, Dockerfile, app_context.md, scoring.toml, test.sh, tools/{score.py,restart_mcp.py}, gates/{render,constraints}/{judge.toml,prompt.md}, scored/{functional,polish,visual}/{judge.toml,prompt.md}; a diff of the file tree against the frozen template shows no added or missing entry outside environment/instructions and solution/app. Nothing required is missing, including tests/app_context.md (3993 bytes, non-empty) and solution/app/server.js. None of the 'Must be absent' items exist: no tests/reward.toml, NOTES.md, SOLUTION.md, .env, zip, spreadsheet, saved run, node_modules, *.db/*.db-wal, __pycache__, *.pyc, *.map, *.bak, *.orig, *~, *.log, .DS_Store or Thumbs.db; the only dotfile is the required tests/.dockerignore; no empty directories. No coverage.json; seed_data.json is the contract's own required asset.

The one candidate for 'build residue' is solution/app/public/ (index.html, runner.html, assets/index.css, assets/index.js at 1,915,385 bytes), which is the Vite output directory (vite.config.mjs: "outDir: 'public', emptyOutDir: true") committed beside its sources (src/, static/, index.html). I judge it required, not residue: solve.sh installs with 'cp -a "$source_app/." "$target/"' and never builds, and server.js line 130 serves only it ('app.use(express.static(path.join(root, 'public'), { dotfiles: 'deny' }));'), so removing it would break the golden. It is also not stale: I copied solution/app to a scratch directory outside the workspace, ran 'npm ci --ignore-scripts' and 'npx vite build' (vite 7.1.7, 35 modules), and the SHA256 of public/assets/index.js, public/assets/index.css, public/index.html and public/runner.html were identical before and after. The bundle carries no sourceMappingURL. src/style.css equals public/assets/index.css (e665bd18...) and static/runner.html equals public/runner.html (ed4a5811...); these are build input and output of one pipeline, not backups. The contract permits 'solution/app/**'.

Limits: the private check-no-stray-files.py and check-required-files.py were not executed; this is a manual application of their documented behaviour. The workbook describes the stray-file checker as rejecting 'build output'; whether its implementation would flag a directory named public/ holding a bundle is unmeasured. That is a deterministic-row question and I found no rule text that makes a required, reproducible prebuilt bundle a defect for this row. Consequence of shipping sources plus bundle: /app receives unused src/, static/, vite.config.mjs, tsconfig.json, package.json and package-lock.json; test.sh needs only /app/server.js and the scripted golden run on these bytes installed through solve.sh and launched successfully, so this has no observed effect.
